candidates.detail: PlacementCandidate::bounds checks local min/max, maps only those two opposite points through a tangent and normalized kitchen axis, then takes their componentwise min and max. That is the enclosing box of the two transformed points, not generally the enclosing box of all four horizontal corners. PlanDirection validates finite nonzero normalization but carries no cardinal restriction.
candidates.conditional_case: For a compact body at origin with ideal kitchen axis (0.6,0.8), tangent (-0.8,0.6), local X in [-0.48,0.48] m and local Z in [-0.9,0.9] m, the two selected corners give architectural X in [-0.156,0.156] m; the full rotated rectangle has X in [-0.924,0.924] m. Local point (-0.45,0.8) maps to (0.84,0.37), inside the intended local rectangle but outside the reported X bounds even after the 0.08 m horizontal clearance margin. These are ideal rational calculations, not executed product f32 or an observed generated state.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: KitchenPair derives the checked axis from a selected wall outward vector. Placement usability uses body bounds with a horizontal clearance margin, then other body, shaft, support, roof and door gates; heating::resolve uses a successful placement to cut a wall and build an assembly, whose part helper turns returned bounds into an axis-aligned cuboid. If an accepted non-cardinal internal candidate reaches those operations, a region of the intended rotated body can fall outside the clearance query and resulting part envelope; a specific missed obstacle, successful full plan or gameplay consequence is not shown. The ordinary grid wall producer uses the four cardinal Direction vectors, for which the two-corner construction is valid. Other wall sources, supported loaded/edited paths, complete audit and generated reachability remain unproved.
